properties.content: Question: can i get covid a 2nd time Answer: Yes, it is possible to get COVID-19 more than once. Reinfection with the virus that causes COVID-19 occurs when someone is infected, recovers, and then gets infected again. While a previous infection can offer some protection against reinfection, it's not a guarantee, and the level of protection can decrease over time. Additionally, new variants of the virus can emerge with the ability to evade existing immunity. Here's why reinfection is possible:: - Immunity wanes: The protection from a previous infection doesn't last forever. The immune response can weaken over time, leaving individuals susceptible to reinfection. - New variants: The virus is constantly evolving, and new variants can emerge that are better at evading the body's immune defenses. - Individual immune responses: People with weakened immune systems may not develop a strong or long-lasting immune response to the virus, making them more vulnerable to reinfection. Even after a previous infection, individuals can still experience severe illness from a reinfection. Staying up-to-date on vaccinations and seeking treatment when symptoms start can help reduce the risk of severe illness and hospitalization, according to the CDC.
